A portrait on display at the National Gallery has left art fans baffled after a mum and daughter noticed something strange

07:00, 09 Sep 2026

A painting exhibited at the National Gallery has left art fans scratching their heads after a mother and daughter spotted what appears to be a Nike trainer.

‌

Portrait of a Boy, crafted by 17th-century Dutch Master Ferdinand Bol, portrays an eight year old lad standing prominently in the foreground, holding a goblet.

‌

The young chap is wearing a black jacket and cape, a white shirt with ruffled sleeves, auburn socks and black boots, all perfectly fitting for the period.

‌

However, upon closer inspection, it seems the boy's shoes feature a white tick remarkably similar to the iconic Nike 'tick' logo.

‌

Considering that Nike was founded centuries after the completion of the portrait, some have suggested that the artwork provides evidence of time travel.

Fiona Foskett noticed the unusual detail while visiting the London gallery with her daughter, Holly.

She said: "I said to my daughter, 'Hold on, is he wearing a pair of Nike trainers?'".

Article continues below

"Looking at the age, he must have got his hands on the first pair of Nike trainers ever made. Or is he actually a time traveller?".

A spokesperson from the National Gallery responded: "We are delighted that this picture has been such a hit with our visitors.

"It resonated with followers when we put out a Tweet asking people to see if they could spot a more 'modern' detail by taking a closer look at the shoes of the eight-year-old boy in the portrait."
